model: Regulated utility dividend discount at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Not deducted separately: the modelled stream is adjusted earnings attributable to NEE, which is already after stock-based compensation expense ($185M cash-flow add-back in FY2025, Metrics.csv / 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement). Deducting it again would double-count.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-09-30 (2,097.6M weighted-average assuming dilution, Q3-2026 10-Q EPS note line 4123; 2,097.3M outstanding at 2026-09-30 on the cover page)
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,097.6M fully diluted (Q3-2026 quarter, includes 8.4M of equity units, options, performance shares and exchangeable notes). Held FLAT. Known non-SBC issuance exists and is NOT modelled in the count: (1) equity units -- stock purchase contracts settling in 2027 and February 2029 (0.4348-0.5435 shares per $50 unit on the 2029 series; $969M of common stock/equity units issued in 9M-2026, $2,038M in FY2025), roughly 1% a year of the count; the growth path is a PER-SHARE adjusted EPS trajectory, which is already net of that dilution, so compounding the count as well would charge it twice. (2) The pending Dominion Energy merger would issue about 716M new NEE shares (0.8138 x ~880M Dominion shares, +34%) -- excluded because the three scenarios are standalone; see deal_analysis.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest dividends. Built in USD: 10-year US Treasury about 5.15% (the 2026-11-13 level used on the folder's other utility builds the same day) + beta 0.70 x 5.0% equity risk premium = 8.65%, rounded up to 8.75%. Beta is set above the 0.60 used for pure regulated holdcos (DUK 8.25%, D 8.0%) because roughly 40% of adjusted earnings come from NEER, a competitive, tax-credit-dependent development business funded 70% with debt and tax equity. Same rate in all three scenarios -- risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not the rate. Cross-check: the FPSC allows FPL 10.95% (range 9.95-11.95%), the regulator's own generous estimate of the same number.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: lease cost and lease interest are inside net income, and no debt of any kind is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: adjusted earnings are attributable to NEE after noncontrolling interests. Note the NCI line is a net LOSS allocated to tax-equity (differential membership) investors ($1,503M in FY2025, $1,425M in 9M-2026), which ADDS to NEE-attributable income -- it is how clean-energy tax credits sold to tax-equity investors reach earnings. NCI on the balance sheet was $11,367M plus $1,477M redeemable at 2026-09-30. Nothing further is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.bvps_memo: Common book value per share $29.32 at 2026-09-30 (61,498 / 2,097.3M). FY2026E adjusted ROE on that book about 13.8%; price/book 2.9x; price / FY2026E adjusted EPS about 21x; dividend yield 2.9%.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. NextEra is a rate-regulated electric utility (FPL, about 60% of adjusted earnings, FPSC-authorised ROE 10.95% under the 2025 rate agreement running January 2026 to at least December 2029, earned 11.7-11.8%) plus NEER, a contracted renewables/storage/transmission developer (about 95% of capacity under long-term contract). The dcf-methods routing table has no utility row, so this was routed on its stated principle -- discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues -- and on the folder's precedent for every rate-regulated US utility (DUK, D, AEP, EXC, ED, AEE, CMS, ETR). A firm-level owner-FCF DCF does not work here: GAAP free cash flow was -$12,121M in FY2025 (operating cash flow $12,485M against $24,606M of capital expenditures, independent power investments and nuclear fuel) and 9M-2026 investment was $27,554M; that spend is rate base and contracted assets funded with new debt, tax equity and equity units, not out of operating cash. Discounting those negative interim flows and then subtracting $108bn of net debt gives the meaningless answer Auckland Airport's first build gave. NEER was considered for a separate owner-FCF leg and rejected: its segment earnings carry an ALLOCATED interest charge (deemed 70% debt), its cash flows are shared with tax-equity partners through HLBV accounting, and its capex ($16.4bn planned 2026) exceeds its cash generation just as FPL's does -- it has the same shape as the utility, so the whole company is valued on one equity stream. What an owner receives is the dividend, and what grows it is adjusted earnings. So: a three-scenario dividend discount model at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt held at ZERO (the flow is after interest; total debt $113,932M = commercial paper 3,716 + other short-term 4,258 + current portion 8,833 + long-term 97,125, and cash $5,579M, are recorded for reference only and must not be subtracted). ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = adjusted earnings attributable to NEE ($M); 'ebitda_margin_path' = dividend payout ratio (%); SBC, D&A, capex, tax and working-capital drivers are all zero because each is already inside net income; 'wacc' = cost of equity; 'terminal_cap_multiple' caps the terminal price-to-dividend multiple (22x = a 4.5% dividend-yield floor). So 'adj_ebitda' and 'fcf' in the projections are DIVIDENDS, and every EBITDA or FCF multiple in the generated file is really a dividend multiple. ANCHORS. Adjusted earnings are derived from the filings' own after-tax adjustment tables (GAAP net income attributable to NEE less non-qualifying hedge gains, XPLR/NEP investment items, decommissioning-fund marks, disposal gains, merger costs): FY2021 $5,021M / $2.55, FY2022 $5,742M / $2.90, FY2023 $6,441M / $3.17, FY2024 $7,063M / $3.43, FY2025 $7,683M / $3.71. 9M-2026: $7,274M / $3.47 against $6,549M / $3.17 (+9.5%); GAAP 9M EPS of $4.82 is inflated by $2,843M of after-tax non-qualifying hedge gains and is not a base. base_revenue 8,474 = FY2026E adjusted EPS $4.04 x 2,097.6M, where $4.04 = 9M actual $3.47 + a fourth quarter of $0.57 (Q4-2025's $0.54 grown about 6%, below the year-to-date pace). No management EPS guidance figure is printed in the extracted 10-K/10-Q text, so FY0 is my estimate, not guidance; replace it when the FY2026 release is in the folder. FY0 is FY2026E, six weeks from complete, so year 1 is FY2027; this ignores the final 2026 quarterly dividend and is slightly conservative. last_fcf 5,229 = annualised dividend $2.4928 ($0.6232 quarterly in each 2026 quarter, +10% on 2025's $2.2664) x 2,097.6M; reported_fcf is set equal to it so the owner-FCF identity holds on this route -- the GAAP free cash flow figure is the -$12,121M above. HOUSE/STREET BAND: collapsed -- SBC is inside the earnings stream on both bases, so there is no separate street value. PENDING MERGER: NEE agreed on 2026-05-15 to acquire Dominion Energy for 0.8138 NEE shares plus a share of $360M cash per Dominion share; both shareholder votes passed September 2026; close targeted H2 2027 subject to FERC, NRC, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina and HSR. NEE is the acquirer, so there is no deal price for its own shares and the deal-completes/deal-breaks routing row does not apply; following the folder's treatment of the Dominion side, the three scenarios are STANDALONE and the deal is carried in deal_analysis. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. Qualitative Analysis JSON was not yet available when this was built; scenario axes are drawn from the 10-K/10-Q directly. DATA GAP: Metrics.csv has no CapEx, FreeCashFlow, dividend or adjusted-EPS columns for NEE and its revenue column is rounded to the nearest $100M from FY2018; capex and dividends were read from the 10-K cash flow statements and not backfilled.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: adjusted EPS 3-year CAGR (FY2022 $2.90 -> FY2025 $3.71), cross-checked against equity_5yr_cagr 8.2% and 9M-2026 adjusted EPS growth of 9.5%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS figures are ADJUSTED EPS, not GAAP: GAAP diluted EPS ($1.48 FY2020, $2.10 FY2022, $3.30 FY2025) gives 16-17% CAGRs that are hedge mark-to-market noise and diverge more than 30% from the equity CAGR. On the adjusted basis EPS, equity and dividends agree within 8-11%.
historical_growth.notes: eps_5yr_cagr is a FOUR-year figure (FY2021 $2.55 -> FY2025 $3.71); FY2020 adjusted earnings are not in the extracted filings. The 'FCF' series on this route is the dividend per share ($1.70 FY2022, $1.87, $2.06, $2.27 FY2025; $2.49 annualised 2026); no 5-year figure because the FY2020 dividend is not in the extracted filings. Equity is the CSV series (total equity including noncontrolling interests: 44,929 FY2020, 48,326 FY2022, 66,479 FY2025). Revenue from the CSV (rounded): 17,000 FY2020, 23,000 FY2022, 25,800 FY2025; revenue is fuel-pass-through and hedge-mark driven and is not the growth anchor. SBC ($185M) is 2% of earnings and growing in line; no SBC-adjusted divergence to flag.

base.narrative: Growth is adjusted-EPS growth; margin is dividend payout. EPS compounds at about 8% through the 2025 rate agreement term (to end-2029), matching the 8.6% of the last three years, then fades to 3.5% as wind and solar tax credits end for projects placed in service after 2030. Payout dips from 61.7% to 59% as dividend growth runs below EPS growth while the capital plan is funded, then recovers to 65%.

bull.narrative: EPS at about 10% through 2029 on large-load demand and storage, fading to 4%; payout held near 60% then rebuilt to 65%.

bear.narrative: EPS growth halves by 2029 and stalls at 2% across the 2030-31 tax-credit cliff and the FPL rate reset; the dividend is defended, so payout drifts up to 66%.

scenario_narratives.base: FPL earns near the top of its 9.95-11.95% band through the 2025 rate agreement (January 2026 to at least December 2029), with about $58.6bn of FPL capital planned for 2026-2030 entering rate base and solar/battery SoBRA step-ups in 2027-2029; Florida customer accounts keep growing about 1.5% a year. NEER converts its approved pipeline (about 11.4GW solar, 4.6GW storage and 3.6GW wind in the $35.6bn 2026-2030 commitment table, front-loaded into 2026-2027 to qualify for credits) and keeps recontracting at acceptable returns. Adjusted EPS grows about 8% to 2029, in line with FY2022-FY2025 (8.6%) and below the 9.5% of 9M-2026. From 2030 growth fades: wind and solar credits lapse for projects placed in service after 2030, the FPL agreement comes up for renewal, and refinancing $114bn of debt at a 5%-plus Treasury takes a rising share of operating income. Dividend growth runs below EPS growth mid-plan (payout 61.7% -> 59%) and payout is rebuilt to 65% as the business matures.
scenario_narratives.bull: Large-load and data-center demand turns NEER's storage, gas-adjacent and nuclear positions into a second growth leg that does not depend on wind and solar credits, and the 2029-2030 lines of the NEER capex table (currently $1.7bn a year, approved projects only) fill in. FPL's 2029 reset preserves a 10.9%-plus ROE and the rate stabilization mechanism (up to about $1.5bn after tax) keeps earned ROE at the top of the band. Rates ease, lowering the cost of the equity-unit and hybrid funding. Adjusted EPS compounds near 10% through 2029 and still 7-8% in 2030-31.
scenario_narratives.bear: Three company-specific things go wrong, none of them exotic. (1) The clean-energy credit cliff: with no credits for wind or solar placed in service after 2030, the tighter begin-construction rules of August 2025 and the foreign-entity restrictions, NEER's new-build economics and tax-equity funding shrink after the 2026-2027 rush and origination falls well short of replacing roll-off. (2) Florida: the motion for reconsideration of the 2025 rate agreement, storm-cost fatigue and bill pressure lead to a harsher 2029 reset -- one regulator sets about 60% of earnings. (3) Funding: $114bn of debt (up from $93bn at December 2025) plus about $12.8bn of tax-equity NCI must be rolled at higher rates, and equity units dilute at a low share price. EPS growth decays from 6% to 2% and settles at 2.5%; the dividend is held, pushing payout to 66%. Not included: a Dominion merger break (termination fee payable by NEE of $4.8bn or $6.5bn in specified circumstances, $2.29-3.10 a share) -- see deal_analysis.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% house default: about 60% of earnings sit under a single state regulator, NEER's growth is tied to federal tax-credit rules that already have a statutory end date, and the balance sheet ($114bn debt, up $21bn in nine months) needs continuous market access at a 5%-plus Treasury. Base 50%: it extends the 8-9% adjusted EPS growth NextEra has actually delivered for four years through a rate agreement that is already in force to 2029. Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs uncontracted large-load demand to convert AND a constructive 2029 Florida reset AND lower rates at the same time.

deal_analysis.status: Pending. Agreement and Plan of Merger signed 2026-05-15; NEE and Dominion shareholder approvals obtained September 2026; requires FERC, NRC, the Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina commissions and HSR clearance. Companies are working to close in the second half of 2027. Source: Q3-2026 10-Q Note 5, NEE_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt lines 3855-3871.
deal_analysis.role: NEE is the ACQUIRER. The valuation above is NextEra standalone.
deal_analysis.consideration: Per Dominion share: 0.8138 NEE shares plus a pro rata share of $360M aggregate cash. Plus more than $2.25bn of proposed bill credits to Dominion customers over two to four years post-close.
deal_analysis.new_shares_basis: 0.8138 x about 880M Dominion shares (the folder's D build uses 879.6-882.1M); about +34% on NEE's 2,097.6M.
deal_analysis.termination_fees: NEE would pay Dominion $4.8bn or $6.5bn in specified circumstances ($2.29-3.10 per NEE share); Dominion would pay NEE about $2.2bn in others.
deal_analysis.house_view: At the folder's own standalone values NextEra is paying with stock the model considers overvalued for a company the model also considers overvalued, so what matters for NEE holders is the RELATIVE exchange. The fixed ratio values a Dominion share at 0.8138 NEE shares; the ratio of the two standalone weighted values (Dominion 55.19 from D_DCF.json of the same date, against this model's NEE weighted value) is what a value-neutral ratio would be. See pro_forma_note, filled from the build output.
deal_analysis.not_modelled: Synergies, the financing of the cash and bill credits, purchase accounting, the Dominion capital plan under NextEra ownership, and any conditions regulators attach. A completed deal makes the combined company about 80% rate-regulated, which would argue for a lower beta than the 0.70 used here.
deal_analysis.pro_forma_note: Illustrative, at house standalone weighted values and before synergies: a value-neutral exchange ratio would be 55.19 / 57.13 = 0.966 NEE shares per Dominion share; NEE is paying 0.8138, i.e. issuing fewer of its own shares than the two standalone values would require. Combined value per share = (57.13 x 2,097.6 + 55.19 x 880 - 360 cash - about 1,780 after-tax bill credits) / (2,097.6 + 716) = about 59.1, roughly +2.0 a share (+3.4%) on the standalone weighted value. The deal is therefore modestly accretive to NEE's intrinsic value on this folder's numbers and does not close the gap to the market price. The standalone weighted value remains the headline; if the deal breaks with NEE paying the fee, deduct 2.29-3.10 a share.

valuation_philosophy.summary: NextEra is valued on the cash an owner actually receives -- the dividend -- growing with adjusted earnings and discounted at an 8.75% cost of equity, because a utility's free cash flow is negative by design while it builds rate base. The method is deliberately unsympathetic to duration: a 3% terminal growth rate at an 8.75% required return capitalises the year-10 dividend at about 18x, an exit P/E near 12x, against roughly 21x today. A market value far above the result therefore says the market is discounting NextEra at closer to 7% or expects high-single-digit growth to persist well past 2030; it does not by itself say the model is wrong. The required-return table shows which.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity dominates: this is a long-duration stream and each 50bp on the cost of equity moves value by roughly 8-10%.
FY0 adjusted EPS ($4.04) is my estimate from 9M actuals, not printed guidance; a 1% miss moves every scenario 1%.

Adjusted earnings exclude non-qualifying hedge marks (+$2,843M after tax in 9M-2026, -$272M in FY2025) and XPLR impairments ($656M FY2025, $852M FY2024, $963M FY2023); the XPLR write-downs were real losses of capital that the adjusted series never charges.

NEER earnings include tax credits monetised through tax-equity partners (the 'net loss attributable to noncontrolling interests' of $1.5bn a year); that source has a statutory end for wind and solar placed in service after 2030.
The Dominion merger would add about 34% to the share count and change the business mix; the standalone values do not describe the combined company.
Per-share growth is assumed net of equity-unit dilution; if issuance runs above about 1% a year the path overstates per-share growth.
Hurricane exposure in Florida is recovered through surcharges, but timing and bill tolerance are regulatory judgments.
